grammar_rules.summary: Dont is used as object of verbs or verbal expressions that include the preposition de, referring to people or things.
grammar_rules.explanation: Il a besoin de ces documents. Voici les documents dont il a besoin. Elle se sert d’un pinceau. Montrez-moi le pinceau dont elle se sert. Tu as parlé d’un souffleur de verre. Où habite le souffleur de verre dont tu nous as parlé? Elle est fière de son fils. Denis est le fils dont elle est fière.
grammar_rules.formation: antecedent + dont + subject + verb (verb requiring de)
restrictions: Only verbs or expressions that include de can be replaced by dont (avoir besoin de, se servir de, parler de).
Dont can refer to people or things, unlike y and en, which are limited to things.
conditions: verb or expression uses preposition de
exceptions: dont is not used when the verb requires à; ce à quoi or the duquel series is used instead
dont also replaces de qui, duquel, de laquelle, desquels, and desquelles
agreement_rules: dont is invariable and does not agree with its antecedent
The verb in the clause agrees with its own subject
grammar_rules.word_order: antecedent + dont + subject + verb (verb requiring de)
transformations: dont replaces duquel, de laquelle, desquels, desquelles in modern French

grammar_rules.summary: Que is used as the direct object of the dependent clause when it already has a subject.
grammar_rules.explanation: Que refers to both people and things and means whom, which, that.
restrictions: Requires the dependent clause to have its own subject
Que is elided to qu' before a vowel or mute h
Cannot serve as the subject; subject function requires qui
conditions: dependent clause has its own subject
exceptions: Requires the dependent clause to have its own subject
que is elided to qu' before a vowel or mute h
Cannot serve as the subject; subject function requires qui
agreement_rules: Que is invariable; it does not agree in gender or number with its antecedent.
Unlike lequel, que carries no gender or number marking, whether the antecedent is a person or a thing.

common_traps: The -e of que is dropped before a vowel (qu')

restrictions: qui is never elided before a vowel or mute h
The verb after qui agrees with the antecedent, not with the speaker
